scenes.title: Narvik Harbour
scenes.description: A photograph from the National Library of Norway shows the harbour in Narvik, dated 17 November 1941. The record does not state a photographer.
scenes.explanation: Personal watercraft with a saddle seat and handlebar steering did not exist in 1941, so nothing in this harbour could be one.
scenes.credit: Mittet & Co. AS via National Library of Norway

scenes.title: Interior during an exhibition
scenes.description: An interior view taken during an exhibition. The photograph is from Europeana and is licensed CC BY-SA.
scenes.explanation: LED desk lamps did not exist in 1928; the first practical visible-spectrum LEDs appeared in the 1960s and domestic LED lamps became common only in the 1990s.

scenes.title: Cannon in a Trench
scenes.description: A cannon is shown in a trench, photographed by Agence Rol in avril 1917. The record notes the subject as Guerre mondiale (1914-1918) -- Guerre de tranchées, and the photograph is held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France, département Estampes et photographie, EI-13 (547).
scenes.explanation: The red-dot reflex sight is a firearm optic that did not exist in 1917, so it cannot be mounted on a field gun of that era.

references.label: Aimpoint - history of the red dot sight

scenes.title: Gambetta's birthday at Les Jardies, Poincaré's speech
scenes.description: A press photograph by Agence Rol showing a speech at the Jardies on 31 March 1912, for the anniversary of Gambetta. It is held by the Bibliothèque nationale de France, département Estampes et photographie.
scenes.explanation: Clip-on lavalier microphones were not available in 1912; they became common only in the later 20th century.

scenes.description: Le retour de grands blessés internés en Allemagne, à la descente du train une collation est distribuée · Bibliothèque nationale de France (Gallica).
scenes.anomaly: modern plastic water bottle with a sports cap
scenes.explanation: Molded clear plastic sports-cap bottles did not exist in 1915; glass and ceramic bottles were used instead.
